result:
The air tasted of saltwater and regret, a familiar tang clinging to the back of my throat. The horizon bled a bruised purple into a twilight sky, the setting sun casting long, fat shadows upon the beach. Familiar ache pulsed in my chest, the rhythm beating time with the ebbing tide. I was scraping another layer of dirt from my sails, my bare hands rough against the weathered planks that once felt like solid, sentient things.  Now, they mirrored my own unsteady spirit.

A dream, echoed through the decades into this cramped, ramshackle boat, had returned to me, a wisp of a memory from a childhood completely forgotten, a lifetime ago. It had been youthful, wild, fueled by the boundless hope of pirates and lost shores. Then, like a ship caught in a storm, it had been crushed, its timbers snapped and splintered, leaving only skeletal memories in its wake. Now, out on these turbulent waters, dreaming again became a defiant act.

I was a ghost, a whisper, a flicker in the periphery of a forgotten world. Who was I? What was my story, anyway? The vesrions of crimson, azure, emerald and gold, writhing on the wind swept sand spun like a kaleidoscope, mocking me in their vibrant fury. The others, they came and went, their stories only whispers on the salt-kissed breeze. Sailors with names etched in a weathered map of the soul, and families who wanted just to be remembered. Strangers who had untied my heart to a phantom image while stealing its name.

My hand trembled, the knife a cold bronze against my palm. It felt wrong, dangerous, almost holy.  It was the legacy, the burden of those who had failed before me. I had inherited their sting, and their sculpted silent stories. They were my victims, my monarchs and my companions, woven into the fabric of my being with threads of betrayal and laughter. Their voices lashed at my ears, their names a chaotic chorus that echoed in my nightmares, even when they were merely ghosts of myself. They clung to me in ways I hadn't anticipated.

 The whoosh of approaching waves vibrated through me, mimicking the rhythmic pulse of a ghost ship. It was a song familiar to every heart that had ever been stolen from its home. A song of tides that turn on desires, of a life that begins and ends in the pale light of vanishing memories. I looked out to the endless horizon, a mirror reflecting a sea of regrets. Here, the only story anyone yearned for was the forever they craved.

How many lives had been reflected on this tangerine orb? The flecks of light that danced across it spoke of dreams put on ice, of secrets locked in chests, of identities stolen and rediscovered in the rain. A million souls, a million whispers, yes, but there was one whispering a different song. 

"There is something wrong here," whispered the rustling of the sails, a shadow reflected in the golden glint of moonlight. Illness, it echoed. Whispered specters of forgotten oceans and fading stars. It was also a form of poetry, death and promise intertwined, like salt and bitter fear.

This vessel was an echo, caught in the eye of a dying hurricane. A reflection of a world that had forgotten how to sleep. 

With each passing day, the fog of my own creation thickened, bringing a growing sense of panic that the landscape of my soul remained the same, unchanging. I didn't remember what good deeds I'd seen. Just what blights and what beauties had otherwise escaped me. The words, my singular purpose, remained elusive. Like a love song long forgotten, the lessons about life hung about me unheeded. 

The wind seemed to sigh, and I heard the voice, soft but distinct, urging me forward. "Is that your ship?" it asked silently, offering a shadow-formed hand to take mine.

And I knew what came next. A bell tolled, and the historians whispered, their ghosting echoes carrying me to the shore.

Gone was the green. Even the golden sands. There was a stillness now, the silence of memories waiting to be told, not heard, waiting for me to write the chapters of their stories.
